reason: E1 demonstrates the synthesis of a Pt-rich shell on a PtCoFeNiCu HEA core via thermal annealing and acid-etching, and reports enhanced electrochemical stability and durability under HDV conditions with lower Pt usage. However, E1 is an electrocatalyst study for ORR, not an automotive exhaust catalyst, and does not address gasoline/hybrid-exhaust conditions with H2O, NO, transient low temperatures, or thermal aging, leaving the key premise of applicability to exhaust catalysis unsupported.
premises: Thermal annealing and acid-etching can form a Pt-rich shell on an HEA core
A Pt-rich shell enhances corrosion resistance and electrochemical stability
The Pt-rich shell structure maintains catalytic activity under harsh conditions
The approach reduces overall Pt consumption while preserving performance
